chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A Muslim does not fulfill a need for another Muslim except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, calls out: 'Upon Me is your reward, and I will not be satisfied for you (as a reward) less than Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for fulfilling a Muslim's need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the immense spiritual weight of 'qada' al-hajah' (fulfilling needs), framing it as a direct divine endorsement. The phrase 'wa la arda laka' (and I will not be content for you) signifies that Allah’s satisfaction is the prerequisite for Paradise, making this act a guaranteed path to Jannah. This underscores the Shia emphasis on social solidarity as a core component of faith, where helping a believer is akin to serving God Himself.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A Muslim will not fulfil a need of the Muslim except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High would Call out: “Upon Me<sup>azwj</sup> is your Reward, and I<sup>azwj</sup> will not be Pleased for you (as a Reward), less than the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whenever a Muslim helps make the wish of a Muslim to come true, Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, says, ‘With Me is your reward and I will not agree to allow it to be less than paradise.’”
